title: Phantom reserved-pool occupancy after deployment causes transient tenant throttles
creator: Asha Menon
description: Multiple customers reported sudden 429s and degraded throughput after a control-plane rollout to the dedicated autoscaler. Initial symptom: tenants with burst credits were denied capacity while dashboards showed reserved pool headroom remaining. This ticket tracks triage, immediate mitigation, root cause analysis, and permanent remediation for a phantom-reservation condition that held back capacity until a node restart or lease reconciliation occurred.
steps_to_reproduce: Deploy autoscaler v2.7.3 with new lease-stamp feature in a staging reserved pool
Simulate tenant burst traffic pattern to exhaust short-term burst tokens
Trigger AZ failover (simulated node bounce) while autoscaler leader election occurs
Observe allocator metrics: allocated_slots vs counted_active_slots diverge and tenant requests are throttled despite reported free headroom
mitigation_actions: Hotpatch rolled: force-release phantom leases via allocator maintenance endpoint (rollout 2026-03-11 04:20 UTC)
Temporarily increased burst_allowance to prevent immediate customer impact for critical tenants
Triggered controlled restarts of affected allocator replicas to clear local cache inconsistencies
root_cause_summary: A race between new lease-stamp reconciliation logic and local KV-cache eviction created transient phantom-occupancy: allocator replicas cached an allocation snapshot that listed slots as occupied while the central ledger had already reclaimed them. During leader handover the allocator reused stale cache entries because the cache eviction window did not account for asynchronous lease invalidation. The autoscaler admission path prioritized local cache reads for latency; this made the miscount visible as reserved capacity being unavailable to admission despite true headroom on other replicas.
patch_notes: PR #4271: add lease-stamp invalidation hook to allocator cache (github.com/redwood/platform/pull/4271)
PR #4283: extend eviction grace to cover leader-election window and add counters for cache-stale events
Backstop: allocator exposes /debug/force_reconcile endpoint to reconcile local cache with central ledger

acceptance_criteria: No reproducible phantom-occupancy in staging across 1000 simulated leader-election events
Deployment baked for 72 hours in Canary pool with telemetry showing cache-stale counter at 0
Add alert: allocator_cache_stale_rate > 0.1% triggers PagerDuty and auto-reconcile runbook
remediation_plan: Merge and deploy PRs to canary reserved-pool (canary rollout 10% of reserved pools)
If canary shows regressions, rollback within 30 minutes and escalate to SRE
After stable canary for 72 hours, gradual rollout to all Dedicated clusters
